decision_reason: Iteration 1 produced strong national-level coverage (CDC HAN advisory, MMWR update, CDC surveillance page, CIDRAP weekly updates, JHU tracker, Wikipedia outbreak article, MSK library guide with county-level detail) and confirmed the primary outbreak locus (Texas/New Mexico/Oklahoma/Kansas Mennonite community). However, several target fields remain underserved by the current candidate set: (1) subnational_location and locality granularity for states beyond Texas — Oklahoma, New Mexico, Kansas, and other states with smaller clusters are represented only in passing; (2) state-level official press releases for Oklahoma (OSDH), New Mexico (NMDOH), and Kansas (KDHE) that would carry authoritative confirmed case counts and dates for those jurisdictions; (3) the Texas DSHS appeared only once and its snippet did not carry Q1 2025 case-count tables; (4) PAHO and WHO appeared (2 results each) but their snippets did not confirm Q1-specific case totals for the US; (5) hospitalization data at the subnational level is absent beyond the MMWR aggregate (85 hospitalized through April 17); (6) the deaths field (3 deaths: 2 children in Lubbock, 1 adult in Lea County, NM) needs corroboration from state-level official sources. A second iteration targeting these specific gaps — state health department pages for TX/NM/OK/KS, PAHO Q1 situation report, and MMWR/CDC early-2025 weekly reports — will materially improve subnational_location, locality, date_reported, deaths, and hospitalizations field coverage within the Q1 2025 window. Budget allows one more iteration (max 4 queries).

Need to surface sources specifically reporting Q1 2025 (Jan–Mar) case counts and dates, particularly early outbreak reports from January–February 2025 for Texas and the initial Oklahoma/NM case announcements.

coverage_assessment:

• disease: Confirmed — Measles, across all accepted sources.
• country: United States — confirmed across all sources.
• subnational_location: Texas (primary), New Mexico (Lea County death confirmed via ArcGIS snippet and nmhealth.org), Oklahoma (OSDH March 11 link via MSK library guide), Kansas (coronavirus.kdheks.gov appeared in iteration 2 domain counts). Maryland (Howard County) also surfaced.
• locality: Gaines County TX, Lubbock TX, West Texas (Mennonite community), Lea County NM, Harris/Houston TX, Rockwall TX, Travis TX, Howard County MD — all identified from snippets.
• date_reported: Multiple Q1 2025 dates captured: January 2025 onset (Wikipedia, MSK guide), February 26 (first TX death — DSHS news release referenced in DSHS snippet, YouTube KSAT12 video, abc7ny.com), March 4 (Lubbock Online — 159 TX cases), March 6 (NM Lea County death — ArcGIS snippet), March 7 (CDC HAN advisory — 208 TX+NM cases), March 21 (Lubbock child care facility index case — MMWR mm7521a1).

• deaths: 3 total confirmed — 2 children in Lubbock (first death Feb 26 per DSHS/abc7ny/YouTube; second death April 6 per DSHS snippet — outside Q1 window), 1 adult in Lea County NM (March 6 per ArcGIS snippet). Within strict Q1 window: at minimum 1 confirmed death (Feb 26 TX child) and 1 confirmed death (March 6 NM adult) = 2 deaths within Q1.
• hospitalizations: 18 hospitalized as of ~Feb 26 (DSHS via abc7ny); 85 hospitalized Jan 1–Apr 17 (MMWR mm7414a1 — partially outside Q1); >99 total (Wikipedia — full outbreak). Q1-specific hospitalization sub-totals will need annotation.
